summary: Persistent 429s in Private VPC after corporate proxy rewrote healthcheck path leading to double accounting
description:
Issue summary:
Customer HelixFin reported persistent 429 responses for a subset of private-vpc API calls during their off-peak batch window after onboarding a corporate HTTP proxy and connection pool. The console showed normal quota remaining while requests were rejected with 429 at the edge.

Impact:
- Intermittent to sustained 429s for background ingestion and SDK heartbeat pings during nightly backfill (estimated 10-20% of requests rejected).
- Customer unable to complete nightly reconciliation within SLA window.
- Visible to monitoring as increased 429 rate on prod-us-east edge-proxy; internal billing counters show excess token consumption.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment (customer-managed control plane)
- Customer uses corporate proxy (forward proxy) performing header normalization and path rewrite policies; uses HTTP/2 multiplexing.
- Traffic routed via private VPC peering to our edge-proxy fleet in us-east region.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Start SDK with keepalive telemetry enabled and background batch workers active (2x workers).
2) Corporate proxy rewrites /hc/health -> /healthcheck/ping and adds X-Forwarded-For chain and reuses connection pools.
3) Nightly backfill triggers; observed 429s within 2-7 minutes.

Observed logs / excerpts:
- Edge-proxy logs: "quota: token_count_increment=2 path=/healthcheck/ping user=helixfin org=12345 source=10.0.0.1" many repeated lines.
- Billing counters: burst credits deducted for small telemetry pings.
- Customer proxy logs show repeated upstream retries for healthcheck endpoints due to probe handling.

Initial hypothesis:
- Corporate proxy is duplicating or replaying healthcheck requests on reuse of HTTP/2 streams, or the proxy rewrite causes our edge to treat the rewritten path as distinct and count both original + rewritten requests against quota because of header mangling.
- Healthcheck/telemetry endpoints are being accounted as billable tokens; repeated probes and connection reuse appear to increment token accounting more than once per logical ping.

Requested by customer:
- Confirm root cause, provide immediate mitigation to stop healthcheck telemetry from consuming burst credits, and guidance to configure proxy to avoid double-counting.
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Martinez (Support): Customer contacted support at 03:12 UTC. Provided request traces and proxy logs. Customer reports spike started after corporate proxy was enabled on 2026-03-09.
2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor (SRE): Acknowledged. Collected edge-proxy request_ids, asked for sample proxied request pcap and full header dump. Requested time window 02:50-03:15 UTC.

2026-03-10 HelixFin (Customer): Uploaded proxy logs and noted the proxy rewrites '/hc/health' -> '/healthcheck/ping' and strips a custom header 'X-Client-Trace'. They are using a shared connection pool with max_conns=200.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor (SRE): Found repeated request_ids where edge consumed quota twice within 200ms. Correlated with HTTP/2 stream reset patterns from proxy. Opened internal ticket INT-3421 to track edge-proxy rate-accounting change.
2026-03-11 Engineering (edge-proxy team): Deployed temporary WAF rule to ignore path '/healthcheck/ping' for quota accounting for this customer. Notified customer of immediate reduction in 429s.

2026-03-12 Sofia Martinez (Support): Customer confirmed night window completed with no further 429 wave. Customer still requests root-cause writeup and permanent config guidance for proxy and for Redwood private deployment to avoid similar issues.

2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor (SRE): Marking ticket Resolved after permanent mitigations merged (edge-proxy PR #5234) and customer-side proxy guidance delivered. Follow-up INT action to harden accounting for rewritten paths.
investigation_notes: Edge trace analysis shows request_id 9f2a3b logged twice with identical body but different upstream Stream IDs (h2 stream 12 and 24).

Billing metric query (2026-03-09 02:45-03:20 UTC): observed 2x token increments for short telemetry payloads compared to baseline. Query: SUM(tokens) GROUP BY minute -> spike aligned with proxy rollout.

Hypothesis validated by reproducer: configuring an in-house test proxy to rewrite path + reuse h2 connection produced duplicate accounting in dev environment. Root cause: edge-proxy assumed one request per h2 stream but proxy behavior led to semi-duplicate upstream frames after RST_STREAM and fast retry. Accounting code incremented on each upstream frame completion, not deduped by idempotency or client-request fingerprint.

Risk assessment: other private customers using similar proxies may be affected if they rewrite paths or reuse connections aggressively; public hosted customers less likely because our public ingress terminates TLS upstream differently.
Temporary mitigation: deployed per-tenant WAF exclusion for healthcheck path and small payload telemetry (non-billable path list).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (2026-03-11): per-tenant path exclusion rule added to WAF to prevent quota accounting for '/healthcheck/ping' and equivalent known telemetry endpoints. Immediate drop in 429s observed in monitoring.

Code fix merged (2026-03-12): edge-proxy PR #5234 changes accounting to use request fingerprint (client-id + trace-id + path) and tolerates rapid RST/RETRY duplicates to avoid double-counting. Backported to private control plane branch and release deployed to HelixFin's tenant.

Customer guidance delivered: (1) Prefer not to rewrite telemetry/healthcheck paths; if rewrite is required, preserve X-Request-Id or custom trace header. (2) Disable aggressive immediate retry for health probes; introduce 100-500ms jitter. (3) When using HTTP/2 pooling, configure the proxy to avoid replaying frames on RST_STREAM for non-idempotent endpoints. Detailed steps attached in Confluence runbook link.

Follow-up: INT-3421 created to add a config knob to private control plane to define a 'telemetry-exempt-path' list and to enhance automated detection of duplicated upstream frames. Engineering estimates 3 sprints for additional hardening.
Status: Resolved for HelixFin. Monitoring scheduled for 7 days to detect regressions. Update: no recurrence in follow-up window as of 2026-03-19 (monitoring note).
